title: Grade 7 Science — Wed, May 20
description: Nutrition in Animals — Day 3 of 5: Enzymes and digestion in detail
subject: science

questions.question: What are enzymes in digestion?
options: Biological catalysts (proteins) that speed up the breakdown of food molecules
questions.explanation: Digestive enzymes are proteins that act as biological catalysts — they speed up the chemical breakdown of food without being consumed.

questions.question: Match enzyme to its substrate: Amylase digests ___
questions.explanation: Amylase breaks down starch into maltose (a simple sugar). It is found in saliva and pancreatic juice.

questions.question: Match enzyme to substrate: Lipase digests ___
questions.explanation: Lipase breaks down fats into fatty acids and glycerol. Pancreatic lipase is the main fat-digesting enzyme.

questions.question: Match enzyme to substrate: Protease (e.g., pepsin, trypsin) digests ___
questions.explanation: Protease enzymes (pepsin in stomach, trypsin from pancreas) break down proteins into amino acids.

questions.question: Why does enzyme activity stop if temperature becomes too high?
options: High temperature denatures (changes shape of) the enzyme, making it non-functional
questions.explanation: Enzymes have a specific shape. Above ~40-50°C, heat breaks the bonds that maintain this shape (denaturation). The enzyme can no longer work.

questions.question: Digestion of starch produces:
questions.explanation: Starch → (amylase) → Maltose → (maltase) → Glucose. The end product of starch digestion is glucose.

questions.question: Digestion of proteins produces:
questions.explanation: Protein → (pepsin/trypsin) → Peptides → (peptidase) → Amino acids. The end products are amino acids.

questions.question: Digestion of fats produces:
questions.explanation: Fat → (lipase, after bile emulsification) → Fatty acids + Glycerol. These are the end products of fat digestion.

questions.question: Which statement is true about digestive enzymes?
options: They are used up in the reactions they catalyse
They can only work at a very specific pH and temperature (optimal conditions)
They work equally well at all temperatures
They are the same as food
questions.explanation: Each enzyme has an optimal pH and temperature. Pepsin works best in acidic stomach conditions; amylase works best at neutral/slightly alkaline pH.

questions.question: The small intestine produces its own enzymes AND receives enzymes from the:
questions.explanation: The pancreas secretes pancreatic juice containing amylase, lipase, and proteases into the small intestine.

questions.question: How does the structure of the small intestine relate to its function?
options: Its long length and villi (finger-like projections) maximise surface area for absorption
Its thick walls prevent nutrient escape
Its narrow diameter speeds up food passage
Its smooth surface prevents food sticking
questions.explanation: The small intestine is ~7 m long with villi and microvilli, creating a huge surface area (like a football pitch!) for absorbing digested nutrients.

questions.question: Absorbed glucose and amino acids enter:
questions.explanation: Glucose and amino acids from the small intestine pass into blood capillaries in the villi, which carry them to the liver and then to all cells.

questions.question: Absorbed fatty acids and glycerol enter:
questions.explanation: Fatty acids and glycerol reform as fats and enter lacteal lymph vessels in the villi, then join the bloodstream via the lymphatic system.

questions.question: After absorption from the small intestine, nutrients are first transported to the:
questions.explanation: Absorbed nutrients go via the hepatic portal vein to the liver. The liver processes, stores, and distributes nutrients to the body.

questions.question: In rumination (cud-chewing) by cows, food is:
options: Chewed, swallowed, and then regurgitated and re-chewed to break down cellulose
questions.explanation: Ruminants (cows, sheep) chew cud — they swallow food into a special stomach, then bring it back to the mouth to chew again. This helps break down tough cellulose in grass.
